text: A small railway station in Gujarat.
A boy helping his father at a tea stall.
Decades later, he would lead the world's largest democracy.
This is the story of Narendra Modi.
Watch till the end. The biggest chapters are still ahead.
Five minutes. Seven decades. One political journey.
From Vadnagar, to Gandhinagar, to New Delhi.
Here's how it happened.
Chapter one. A boy from Vadnagar.
Narendra Damodardas Modi was born on the seventeenth of September, nineteen fifty, in Vadnagar, a small town in Gujarat.
His family was poor. His father ran a tea stall at the local railway station.
Modi has said that as a boy, he helped there, serving tea to passengers on passing trains.
At about eight years old, he was introduced to the R S S, a Hindu nationalist volunteer organisation.
It would shape the rest of his life.
But as a teenager, he did something unexpected. He left home.
Chapter two. The wandering years.
By his own account, he spent about two years travelling across India.
He has spoken of time in the Himalayas, searching for purpose.
When he returned, he moved to Ahmedabad, and in nineteen seventy one, became a full time worker for the R S S.
Chapter three. The organiser.
For years, he worked behind the scenes, building networks across Gujarat.
During the Emergency of the nineteen seventies, he went underground to avoid arrest.
In nineteen eighty seven, he became the organising secretary of the B J P in Gujarat.
In nineteen ninety one, he helped organise the Ekta Yatra, a march from Kanyakumari in the south, to Srinagar in the north.
By nineteen ninety eight, he was a national general secretary of the B J P.
Halfway there. And the biggest moments are still ahead.
Coming up: power, controversy, and a landing on the Moon.
Chapter four. Chief Minister of Gujarat.
In January two thousand one, a massive earthquake struck Gujarat, killing around twenty thousand people.
That October, Modi became the state's Chief Minister, without ever having held elected office.
Months later, in two thousand two, communal riots in Gujarat killed more than a thousand people.
His government's handling of the violence drew strong criticism at home and abroad. An investigation appointed by the Supreme Court later found no evidence to prosecute him.
He went on to win three straight state elections, and became Gujarat's longest serving Chief Minister.
Next: the national stage.
Chapter five. Prime Minister.
In twenty fourteen, the B J P won two hundred and eighty two seats, the first single party majority in thirty years.
On the twenty sixth of May, Modi was sworn in as India's fourteenth Prime Minister.
His government launched campaigns like Clean India, Jan Dhan bank accounts, Make in India, and Digital India.
In twenty sixteen, it suddenly withdrew five hundred and one thousand rupee notes. The move is still debated today.
In twenty seventeen, it introduced a nationwide Goods and Services Tax.
Chapter six. The world stage.
In twenty nineteen, the B J P won again, with three hundred and three seats.
That August, the government revoked the special status of Jammu and Kashmir.
During the pandemic, India gave more than two billion vaccine doses.
In August twenty twenty three, Chandrayaan three became the first mission to land near the Moon's south pole.
That September, New Delhi hosted the G twenty summit, where the African Union joined as a permanent member.
In twenty twenty four, he won a third straight term, the first Prime Minister to do so since Jawaharlal Nehru.
This time, the B J P fell short of a majority on its own, and governs with its allies.
From a tea stall at a railway station, to the world stage.
Admired by many, criticised by many, his journey has reshaped Indian politics.
